author: NorthEast News Desk
body: An 83-year-old man was arrested during a joint police operation at Cathedral Pines, a wooded recreation area shared by Essex and Manchester-by-the-Sea. NBC10 Boston reported Friday that the operation followed complaints about inappropriate activity in the area, including a report that someone had grabbed another visitor and behaved lewdly.

Police from both communities assigned plainclothes and uniformed officers to the property. Authorities said the man was taken into custody after propositioning a detective during the patrol. His name and the specific charge were not included in the initial public report, and officials did not say whether he was suspected in the earlier grabbing allegation.

The arrest comes as the two departments increase their presence at Cathedral Pines in response to visitor concerns. Police said the patrols are intended to deter misconduct and keep the public recreation area accessible. The reported conduct remains under investigation, and an arrest is not a finding of guilt. Visitors who witness threatening, unwanted or illegal behavior should leave the immediate area when safe and contact local police with the time, location and description of what occurred.
dek: A joint Essex and Manchester-by-the-Sea patrol followed complaints about inappropriate activity in the wooded recreation area.
headline: Joint patrol leads to arrest at Cathedral Pines recreation area
